title_clean: Rise and Fall of a Great Fund Manager
summary: Unnamed Kerala micro-cap fund manager parable: skill was real, but capacity was not. TV fame pulled in huge AUM (700→1,400 crore said to double within a week of a house showcase, peak ~2,000 crore); his own buying propelled micro-cap prices, manufacturing an illusion of genius; copycat clients paid the minimum fee only to mirror his buys with 10-20x their own capital (true exposure ~20,000-40,000 crore); the 2018 small-cap crash exposed zero liquidity. Portfolio sizing rule: ~5-10% micro-cap, 20-25% mid-cap, 50-60% large-cap.
lessons: Strategy capacity is finite: a skill that works with 50 crore fails with 2,000 crore - size capital to the strategy's arena.
A fund's own buying can propel illiquid micro-cap prices, faking alpha; the illusion unwinds in the crash.
Copycat investors who mirror a fund's disclosed buys multiply real exposure far beyond AUM, deepening the eventual exit trap.
Allocation rule of thumb: ~5-10% micro-cap, ~20-25% mid-cap, ~50-60% large-cap.
Comfort breeds risk escalation: a lender who started at 50,000 rupees ended at 50 lakh because early repayment created false confidence.

title_clean: Why NIFTY May Hit 22,000 by Oct 2024 - Hot Take
summary: Bullish roadmap to Nifty 22,000 by Oct-2024 Diwali: two years of zero index return (18,600 Oct-2021 to ~19,000) plus FD-parity math imply ~30% catch-up; long consolidation precedes powerful breakouts; FII India-bear/China-bull trade failed (China still below pre-Lehman level while Nifty sextupled from 3,000), FIIs reversing with 30,000+ crore cash buying in a month; heavyweights (Infosys, TCS ~20% below highs, HDFC twins, Reliance rangebound) lag a broad rally and can add fuel; macro improving (record GST, bond-index inclusion, PMI >60). Track-record framing: 2020 '7,500 or 15,000 first' call, gold $3,000 rebuttal, Moneycontrol 19,000/20,500-21,000 targets; 'mathematician, not a magician'; 'neither bull nor bear, a chameleon'.
lessons: Long consolidation zones historically resolve in powerful breakouts - two-year ranges set up outsized moves.
Mean-reversion parity: if the index gives zero return while FDs compound, subsequent bull legs historically over-compensate to restore equity premium.
FII India-bear/China-bull rotation failed for 15 years; forced reversals of such flows become tailwinds.
A market reaching highs on narrow breadth can accelerate when lagging heavyweights catch up.
Prediction discipline: state reasoning, accept fallibility, and let changing data change the view.
